reasoning:
The code-level mechanism reproduces: printHexu32imm (NVPTXInstPrinter.cpp:444-448) uses the signed formatHex(int64_t) overload on a sign-extended immediate and appends 'U', so prmt selectors with bit 31 set print as '-0x...U' (llc emits -0x1U for selector -1, -0x80000000U for 0x80000000, -0x10000U for 0xFFFF0000, vs correct 0x7654U for a positive selector). However this is NOT a bug under the required standards.

(1) NOT a miscompile. The candidate's claim that the text "no longer represents the IR constant's 32-bit pattern" is false. Per the PTX ISA (authoritatively quoted): integer literals are non-negative; unary minus is a constant-expression operator that PRESERVES the operand's signed/unsigned type; all PTX integer constants are 64-bit and are CONVERTED to the operand's size at use. So '-0x1U' = unary-minus of the .u64 literal 1 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, truncated to the 32-bit selector operand = 0xFFFFFFFF — exactly the intended value. Likewise -0x80000000U -> 0x80000000 and -0x10000U -> 0xFFFF0000. Moreover prmt only uses the LOW 16 BITS of the selector (LLVM NVPTXUsage docs + PTX ISA), which are identical in every case. There is no concrete defined input where the emitted PTX computes a different prmt result than the IR. The title's own framing ("-0x1U instead of 0xffffffffU") names two textual forms that are EQUAL IN VALUE under PTX, which is exactly why it is not a miscompile.

(2) NOT an assertion/segfault. llc does not crash; it emits valid-looking PTX.

(3) The "ptxas rejects it" claim is unsubstantiated. PTX explicitly allows constant expressions (incl. unary minus) as instruction operands, so '-0x1U' is grammatically a valid operand. ptxas is unavailable in this environment and web search found no confirmation of rejection; I cannot assert a build failure.

I also disproved the suggestion that the backend's to_sign_extend_selector SDNodeXForm auto-triggers this: that xform builds a 16-bit value (concat of four 4-bit nibbles, BSext in 0x8-0xB), producing selectors 0x8880-0xBBB3 — checked into i8x4-instructions.ll as positive 0x8880U/0x9991U/0xbbb3U, NEVER bit-31-set. The bit-31 path requires a user-supplied direct @llvm.nvvm.prmt selector >= 0x80000000.

Conclusion: at most a cosmetic non-canonical-output nit (sibling printHexUImm masks and uses the unsigned overload to print 0xffffffffU); not a correctness bug.
expected: Canonical/preferred output would mask to 32 bits and use the unsigned overload, e.g. 0xffffffffU, 0x80000000U, 0xffff0000U, 0x7654U (matching sibling printHexUImm). But the emitted '-0x1U' etc. are NOT wrong in value: under PTX ISA constant-expression rules (unary minus preserves the .u64 type; 64-bit constant converted/truncated to the 32-bit operand) '-0x1U' evaluates to 0xFFFFFFFF, '-0x80000000U' to 0x80000000, '-0x10000U' to 0xFFFF0000 — identical to the intended selector, and prmt uses only the low 16 bits regardless. So the emitted code is value-correct; the difference from the canonical form is purely cosmetic.

Every f16 value, including subnormals, widens to a NORMAL f32 (smallest f16 subnormal = 2^-24, far above smallest normal f32 = 2^-126), so the f32 result of fpext is never subnormal and result-flushing has no licensed effect. The only thing `.ftz` does on this widening cvt is corrupt the f16 input. Concrete defined input: half 0xH03FF (largest f16 subnormal = 1023*2^-24 = 6.097555e-05). Correct fpext result = 6.097555e-05 (a normal f32, bits 0x387FC000, exponent field 112); the emitted cvt.ftz.f32.f16 flushes the subnormal f16 input to +0.0. The f32 denormal-mode flag governs f32 denormals, not f16 denormals, so flushing the f16 input based on it is wrong even under the FTZ contract; the corroborating asymmetry is that f16->f64 correctly emits no-ftz cvt.f64.f16. ptxas accepts cvt.ftz.f32.f16 (LLVM D51042 only removed rounding-mode ftz cvt variants; this no-rounding-mode form is intentionally retained and tested in f16-instructions.ll:797), so the bad instruction reaches hardware.

Adversarial caveat: the candidate also claims the bf16->f32 case is a bug, but that is incorrect: bf16 shares f32's exponent range, so bf16 subnormals ARE subnormal in f32, and cvt.ftz.f32.bf16 flushing a bf16 subnormal yields an f32 result that genuinely would have been a subnormal f32 -- arguably within the f32-FTZ contract the user opted into. I therefore do NOT rely on the bf16 case. The miscompile is specific and airtight for f16->f32 only. Confidence is 0.88 rather than higher because the FTZ flush is a user-opted relaxation and one could argue (weakly) that flushing the narrow input is an acceptable consequence of fast-math; but the f32-specific denormal flag has no semantic authority over f16 denormals and the IR-level fpext is exact, so the wrong knob is clearly being applied.
expected: Plain `cvt.f32.f16 %r1, %rs1;` (no .ftz), as emitted with the default IEEE f32 denormal mode. fpext half to float is exact: for half 0xH03FF the result must be 6.097555e-05 (f32 bits 0x387FC000, a NORMAL f32), not +0.0. Because every f16 value widens to a normal f32, no f32 denormal is ever produced, so the f32 FTZ setting provides no license to flush; the f16->f32 fpext pattern should never set the FTZ bit (matching the f16->f64 / bf16->f64 extends, which correctly have no ftz variant).

refute.reasoning:
Reproduced the exact output (cvt.ftz.f32.f16) and confirmed the IR is verifier-clean (no UB). The claim is REFUTED because its central premise about PTX semantics is wrong.

The verifier asserts that .ftz on cvt.ftz.f32.f16 flushes the f16 INPUT subnormal to zero, corrupting the exact widening. The authoritative PTX ISA 8.7 (page 264, cvt "Subnormal numbers"/"Floating Point Notes") states explicitly: "Modifier .ftz may be specified to flush single-precision subnormal inputs and results to sign-preserving zero. Modifier .ftz can only be specified when either .dtype or .atype is .f32 and applies only to single precision (.f32) inputs and results." For cvt.f32.f16 the source is f16 (.atype), which is NOT single-precision, so .ftz does NOT flush it. .ftz acts only on f32 inputs and f32 results.

For the claimed concrete input half 0xH03FF (largest f16 subnormal = 6.097555e-05), I computed the f32 result = bits 0x387fc000, exponent field 112 — a fully NORMAL f32 (well above smallest normal f32 = 2^-126). The verifier itself concedes every f16 widens to a normal f32. So: (a) .ftz does not touch the f16 input (not single-precision), and (b) the f32 result is normal so result-flushing has nothing to do. Therefore cvt.ftz.f32.f16 produces exactly 6.097555e-05, identical to cvt.f32.f16. The claimed +0.0 output never occurs; there is no miscompile.

The verifier's reasoning rests entirely on misreading "subnormal inputs" as "any subnormal input" rather than the spec's explicit "single-precision (.f32) inputs." The cvt.ftz.f32.f16 form is intentional, tested NVPTX behavior (f16-instructions.ll lines 185-186) precisely because it is value-equivalent to the non-ftz form for narrow inputs. Confidence 0.95 (not higher only because I could not run ptxas/hardware to empirically execute the instruction, but the PTX ISA wording is unambiguous and authoritative).

title: FTZ applied to fpext f16/bf16 -> f32 flushes the (sub)normal narrow input, miscompiling exact widening conversions to 0.0
